abstract: A radioimmunoassay for urinary human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) which used antiserum to the hCG beta carboxy-terminal peptide was employed to detect hCG production in women with gestational trophoblastic disease. The urinary hCG assay was considerably more effective in detecting increased hCG production, and, hence, persistent tumor burden, than the commonly used serum hCG beta subunit radioimmunoassay. In two women treated for choriocarcinoma, urinary hCG levels remained distinctly elevated for 2 to 6 weeks, even though the serum hCG level was undetectable; in both cases, the urinary hCG radioimmunoassay reliably predicted the eventual reappearance of hCG in the serum. In six women whose disease remitted, the urinary hCG level declined to the normal range during chemotherapy, and remained there afterward. In eight patients who had been in remission for periods of from 1 to 14 years, urinary hCG levels were in the normal range. We conclude that this highly sensitive and reliable method for the detection of hCG production improves the ability to diagnose persistent trophoblastic disease.
abstract_ja: hCGのβカルボキシ末端ペプチドに対する抗血清を用いた放射免疫測定法により、妊娠性絨毛性疾患の女性における尿中ヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)産生を検出した。この尿中hCG測定法は、一般的に用いられている血清hCGβサブユニット放射免疫測定法よりも、hCG産生の増加、すなわち持続する腫瘍量の検出に有効であった。絨毛癌で治療を受けた2名の女性では、血清hCGが検出されなくなった後も2〜6週間にわたり尿中hCGは明らかに高値を示し、いずれの症例でも血清hCGの再出現を正確に予測した。寛解した6名の女性では、化学療法中に尿中hCG値が正常範囲まで低下し、その後も正常範囲にとどまった。寛解期間が1〜14年に及ぶ8名の患者では、尿中hCG値は正常範囲内であった。この高感度で信頼性の高いhCG産生検出法は、持続性絨毛性疾患の診断能を向上させるとわれわれは結論する。
